title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — same split for Adam: act in paradise vs imputation; propagation suffices
pass_a_gloss: Split 'when did we sin in Adam?' the same way: when Adam ate in paradise; and when his sin is 'ours.' Imputation is not required to say we sinned in him—propagation of the vice is enough: when we were born corrupted from him.
pass_b_english: But if you similarly resolve the question, When did we sin in Adam? into these two, When did Adam sin? and, When is his sin imputed to us? the answer to the first will be easy, when he ate the forbidden fruit in paradise; to the second, not to say that imputation is supposed, whereas yet, that we may be said to have sinned in Adam, imputation is not necessary, propagation of sin suffices, I answer, when we were begotten of Adam vitiated and corrupted.
source_text: Quod si similiter resolvas quaestionem, Quando peccavimus in Adamo? in has duas, Quando peccavit Adamus? &, Quando imputatur nobis eius peccatum? Facilis erit responsio ad primam, quando manducavit fructum vetitum in paradiso; ad secundam, ut taceam supponi imputationem, cum tamen, ut dici possimus peccasse in Adamo, non sit necessaria imputatio, sufficiat propagatio peccati, respondeo, quando geniti sumus ab Adamo vitiati & corrupti.

choices.choice: Act in paradise vs ours by propagation at birth; imputation not required
